item.title: Iran approves humanitarian passage as Hormuz yuan toll system takes shape
item.description:
Iran has extended an invitation to European, Asian, and Arab nations to negotiate formal transit agreements through the Strait of Hormuz, the latest escalation in a standoff that is reshaping how global oil moves and how it is paid for. The offer, announced this week by Head of the Government Information Council Elias Hazrati on Iranian state television, came as vessels already transiting the strait under Iranian escort are settling fees in Chinese yuan and stablecoins rather than U.S. dollars.

"Iran fully controls the Strait of Hormuz," Hazrati said. "We will invite European, Asian and Arab countries that want to use it to conclude an agreement with us."

item.title: WHO warns of nuclear accident risk as Iran war deadline looms
item.description: President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Iran on Saturday demanding it reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating consequences, as the conflict now in its sixth week showed no signs of abating. Iran's military dismissed the warning and vowed that "the gates of hell" would open if the United States followed through on its threats.

item.title: Trump says Putin has 'zero fear' of NATO in Easter tirade
item.description: President Donald Trump escalated his attacks on NATO on Easter Sunday, telling ABC News that his earlier calls for the alliance to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz were merely "a test" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin has "zero fear" of the military bloc. The remarks, made during phone calls from his Virginia golf club, mark the latest salvo in a week of increasingly hostile rhetoric toward America's closest allies.

item.title: Iran denies refusing Pakistan-hosted talks with US
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi pushed back on Saturday against reports that Tehran had refused to participate in Pakistan-hosted peace talks, insisting that "we have never refused to go to Islamabad" and expressing gratitude for Pakistan's mediation efforts, even as the gap between Washington and Tehran's positions remains vast.

item.title: Iran strikes hit UAE, Kuwait infrastructure as Gulf attacks enter sixth week
item.description: Iranian drone and missile attacks struck civilian infrastructure across the Persian Gulf on Sunday, damaging a major petrochemical plant in Abu Dhabi, targeting a port in Sharjah, and setting fire to oil facilities in Kuwait, as Tehran's campaign of retaliation against Gulf states entered its sixth week.

item.title: Dar, Araghchi discuss de-escalation as Iran denies talks have stalled
item.description: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar spoke by phone with Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi on Saturday to discuss the regional crisis, with Dar reaffirming Islamabad's commitment to de-escalation and the importance of resolving the conflict through dialogue, according to a Foreign Office statement. The two leaders agreed to maintain close contact as diplomatic efforts continue.

item.title: Trump delays Iran ultimatum again after US rescues downed airman
item.description:
President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden ultimatum to Iran on Sunday, threatening to strike the country's bridges and power plants unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz, hours after U.S. Special Operations forces successfully extracted the second crew member of an American fighter jet shot down over southern Iran.

The rescue and Trump's escalating rhetoric mark a turning point in the six-week-old conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran, which has engulfed Gulf states in a widening campaign of missile and drone strikes and triggered a global energy crisis.

item.title: Russia's Ust-Luga port resumes crude loading after drone strikes
item.description: Russia's key Baltic oil export hub at Ust-Luga resumed crude loading on Saturday after days of disruption caused by repeated Ukrainian drone strikes, according to Bloomberg News. The Aframax-class vessel The Jewel began cargo loading at the port, citing shipping data seen by Bloomberg, marking the first sign of recovery at a facility that had been largely shut down since late March.

item.title: Trump threatens to bomb Iran's infrastructure in Easter ultimatum
item.description: Global financial markets face a turbulent week after President Donald Trump used Easter Sunday to issue an expletive-laden ultimatum to Iran, threatening to destroy the country's power plants and bridges if it does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his April 7 deadline. The threats, combined with a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report and a stark warning from the International Monetary Fund, have created a volatile cocktail of rising oil prices, falling equities, and dimming hopes for interest rate relief.

item.title: Artemis II crew tests survival suits as Moon flyby nears
item.description: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission spent their fifth day in space Sunday testing the orange Orion Crew Survival System suits they would depend on in an emergency, as the spacecraft closed within roughly 60,000 miles of the Moon ahead of a historic flyby set for Monday afternoon.

item.title: Study finds first evidence of 'forbidden' black hole mass gap
item.description: A trio of recent discoveries is reshaping how astronomers understand the violent ends of stars, from the heaviest stellar explosions ever theorized to aging suns that devour their own worlds and dead stars with puzzling split personalities.

item.title: Trump says NATO appeal on Hormuz was a deliberate 'test'
item.description:
President Donald Trump told ABC News that his appeals for NATO allies to help patrol the Strait of Hormuz were never a genuine request but rather a deliberate test of the alliance's resolve — one he says it failed.

"This was a test for NATO, I didn't need them, but I wanted to test them," Trump said in an interview with ABC News correspondent Rachel Scott published Sunday. "They're a paper tiger. Paper Tiger. They have no ships. They have nothing, and Putin has zero fear of them. But I did it as a test."

The remarks are the latest in weeks of escalating rhetoric from Trump against the transatlantic defense pact, which he has criticized for refusing to join U.S. military operations against Iran. Trump first told Britain's Telegraph in an interview published April 1 that leaving NATO was "beyond reconsideration," calling allies "cowards" for declining to help reopen the strategic waterway.

item.title: Iran allows 15 ships through Hormuz in highest daily count since blockade
item.description: Iran permitted 15 vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours after granting them official clearance, according to Iran's semi-official Fars News Agency, as reported by The Wall Street Journal on Sunday. The uptick marks the highest single-day count since Tehran imposed a selective blockade on the strategic waterway in mid-March, though maritime traffic remains a fraction of normal volumes.

item.title: Gulf funds near $24B deal to back Paramount's Warner takeover
item.description:
Paramount Skydance is nearing a $24 billion equity commitments from three Gulf sovereign wealth funds to finance its $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, in a move that would resolve weeks of uncertainty over whether Middle Eastern capital would remain part of the deal.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is contributing approximately $10 billion, the largest individual commitment, alongside investments from the Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi-based L'imad Holding Co., according to the report. The Gulf investors will hold minority, non-voting stakes, and Paramount does not expect the arrangement to trigger review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States.

item.title: Koch becomes farthest-traveling woman as Artemis II nears moon
item.description:
NASA astronaut Christina Koch has officially become the woman who has traveled the farthest from Earth, surpassing the distance records of every female astronaut before her as the Artemis II mission hurtles toward a lunar flyby scheduled for Monday.

Koch, 47, is one of four crew members aboard the Orion spacecraft — named Integrity — which launched from Kennedy Space Center on April 1 at 6:35 p.m. EDT. She passed the milestone on approximately April 3 as Orion left Earth orbit and entered its trans-lunar trajectory, moving well beyond the roughly 250-mile altitude of the International Space Station where all previous female astronauts had flown.

item.title: IRGC says Hormuz will 'never return' as Trump deadline looms
item.description: Iran allowed 15 ships to transit the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours under its permission-based corridor system, even as President Donald Trump set a Tuesday deadline threatening to strike Iranian power plants and bridges if the waterway is not fully reopened. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy declared Sunday that the strait will "never return to its former state, especially for the US and Israel," signaling Tehran's intent to permanently reshape control over one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints.

item.title: Iran hits Gulf infrastructure as Trump's 48-hour deadline nears
item.description: Iran launched a new wave of missiles and drones at Gulf countries early Sunday, striking infrastructure across the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia as the conflict that began on February 28 entered its sixth week. The attacks came one day after President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum for Tehran to reach a deal or face intensified strikes.

item.title: Artemis II crew begins historic lunar flyby Monday
item.description: Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are poised to sweep around the Moon on Monday, capping a five-day outbound journey and marking the first time humans have traveled to the lunar neighborhood since Apollo 17 in 1972. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency — launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1 at 6:35 p.m. EDT aboard the Space Launch System rocket.

item.title: Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen Strait of Hormuz arrives Monday
item.description:
Global oil prices climbed again over the weekend, with U.S. crude rising above $114 per barrel and Brent crude topping $110, after President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden ultimatum demanding Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz by the end of Monday or face strikes on its civilian infrastructure.

The latest price spike comes as the U.S.-Iran conflict enters its sixth week with no resolution in sight, and as Trump's self-imposed April 6 deadline for Iran to restore access to the critical waterway arrives.

item.title: Study: 84% of fire-vulnerable species face rising wildfire risk by 2100
item.description: Climate-driven wildfires will place nearly 84 percent of fire-vulnerable species at heightened risk by 2100, according to a study published in Nature Climate Change on April 5. The research, led by Xiaoye Yang of the University of Gothenburg, offers one of the most comprehensive assessments to date of how shifting wildfire regimes could reshape threats to global biodiversity.
